**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Broad tomato leaf with numerous very small (1-3mm) dark/black angular lesions scattered across the surface, plus white granular deposits
- **Bacterial Speck reference**: Very similar — small dark spots on tomato leaf, sometimes with faint yellow halos. Pattern matches closely
- **Septoria reference**: Spots are larger with lighter centers — doesn't match the tiny dark specks
- **Alternaria reference**: Was a microscopy image, not field-comparable
- **Powdery Mildew reference**: Shows distinct white fluffy colonies with central necrosis — white deposits in test are more granular/scattered, not fluffy patches

The small dark angular specks are most characteristic of Bacterial Speck. The scattered white granular material may be pesticide residue or early sporulation but is not the defining feature. Bacterial Speck's defining symptom — tiny (1-3mm) very dark, often angular leaf spots on tomato — aligns best with the test image.
